bib.title: Fast Inference of Mixture-of-Experts Language Models with Offloading

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; figure plots not read (values not in text).

question: How can large sparse MoE language models such as Mixtral-8x7B generate tokens interactively on consumer GPUs with limited memory?
hypothesis: MoE experts show locality between adjacent tokens and early hidden states predict later experts, so an LRU cache plus speculative expert loading will speed up offloaded inference.
contributions: observe expert reuse between adjacent tokens and that early-layer hidden states predict later-layer experts
MoE-specific offloading strategy: LRU expert cache and speculative expert loading
practical combination of mixed quantization and offloading to run Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct at 2-3 tokens per second on a T4, RTX 3060 and RTX 3080 Mobile

method.summary: Experts are kept in an LRU cache of k experts per layer on the GPU, the rest in pinned host RAM. After loading the current layer's experts, the next layer's gate is applied to the current hidden states to guess 1-2 experts to prefetch. Attention layers are quantized to 4-bit and experts to 2- or 3-bit with HQQ.
method.task: interactive (batch size 1) token generation with offloaded MoE LLM

models.name: Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct
models.architecture: sparse MoE decoder, 8 experts, 2 active per token
models.layers: inferred: 32, from Figure 2 layer axis 0-30 and per-layer experts; not stated

inference.decoding: pure sampling proportional to predicted probabilities, no temperature or nucleus sampling

parameters.LRU cache size k: 2 for 12GB GPUs (RTX 3060), 4 for 16GB GPUs; same k per layer
parameters.speculative prefetch: 1-2 most likely experts, triggered right after current layer's experts finish loading; prefetched experts do not evict cached ones
parameters.quantizer: HQQ; attention 4-bit; experts 2-bit (group size 16, scale group 128, ~2.6 bits/param) or 3-bit (group 64, scale group 128); 4-bit is group 64, scale group 256; embeddings, logits, gates, norms 16-bit
parameters.hardware tested: T4 Colab 16GB PCIe3; RTX 3080 Mobile 16GB PCIe4; RTX 3060 12GB PCIe3; A100-80GB-SXM; Azure T4 for 3-bit

metrics.name: expert recall / cache hit rate
metrics.definition: fraction of times an expert needed for inference was already on GPU

metrics.name: tokens per second
metrics.definition: average tokens generated per second, batch size 1

baselines: naive offloading (accelerate) loading the entire MoE layer
eval.protocol: single configuration per cell; no seeds, repeats or variance reported

evidence.quote: We use k = 2 for RTX 3060 and k = 4 for all other GPUs.

limits: No hit-rate or recall numbers are given in the text; only plotted in Fig 2.
Single runs, no variance, seeds or number of conversations/tokens stated.
Speed measured only at batch size 1; prompt-encoding phase not measured separately.
LRU is simple: ignores frequency, per-layer cache size or sequential patterns; speculative loading tested only with Mixtral gating.
Quantization is data-free HQQ only; authors believe GPTQ/AWQ would give similar conclusions but did not test.
3-bit run uses a different machine (Azure T4) than 2-bit (Colab T4), so not strictly comparable.
Naive offloading cell for 3060 3-bit looks anomalous.
No limitations section; the paper is a short preprint, and the Mixtral-specific results may have dated.
